what: The schema of the published file (docs/html/api/gates.json) and of the sources in gates/. It is not decoration: build/gates_validate.mjs interprets it, and it is what rejects an extra field, a wrong type or a value outside its enum. A new field is declared here first.

history.1: The definition the tool carried compiled in src/urazuke/catalog.ts until 2026-10-23. One evaluator per step, in a field named `evaluator`.
history.2: The method takes ownership (D-050). Each step declares a LIST of evaluators with their since_schema; the forty-five rules of Annex H, the adapters and the D-042 additions the tool did not measure come in.

editing_rules.ascii_only: The data layer is English and pure ASCII (no character above 0x7F), sources and published file alike, and the validator enforces it (D-051). English is the canonical language of the profession, and whatever is not translated is published in it; translating for the comprehension of an end user is the consumer tool job, not this file job. The single exception is the frozen base: its text comes from gates/baseline.json, is in the Spanish of the method, and is not edited here.
editing_rules.base_is_frozen: An entry without since_schema comes from the freeze in gates/baseline.json and has to stay identical to it. A new requirement is added as a NEW entry with its since_schema; the old one is not edited. That is what makes zero difference demonstrable.
editing_rules.ids_append_only: Steps, stations, rules (CQ-*, UX-*) and evaluator names are added: never recycled, never renamed, never changed in meaning.
editing_rules.single_copy_of_each_text: The statement of every rule lives ONLY in Annex H. gates/heuristics.json carries the pointer and the build extracts the text from the English version of the annex. Transcribing it here would be the second copy that step 11 hunts down.
editing_rules.nothing_invented: A threshold the owner did not declare is published with value null and declared:false. Never with a factory value disguised as a default.
editing_rules.version_is_declared: The version is declared by hand and bound to its content. Changing a covered key without raising catalog_version is rejected (E_VERSION), and so is recording a hash that is not the one the content produces.
editing_rules.language_is_declared: The language of each text is declared in catalog.json#languages.text_language and checked on every build: every text the rule calls Spanish has to be literally in the frozen base. The file is bilingual because the base is not edited, and saying so is the difference between a consumer that can translate for its reader and one that shows Spanish to an English reader.
editing_rules.provenance_is_declared: Every entry the method added after the freeze declares since_version: the published catalog_version in which it first appeared. since_schema says which schema an entry belongs to and is too coarse to compute an upgrade -- it only separates the frozen base from everything added later. since_version is what makes the differential between two published versions computable without guessing, which is what a project that pinned one of them needs before deciding to raise it.

version_scheme.catalog_version: Declared BY HAND by the method in gates/catalog.json, in the 2026.10.1 style. It is what a project freezes, and what has to read back the same two years from now.
version_scheme.content_hash: Computed by the build over the canonicalised payload and published. The consumer RECOMPUTES it and compares: that way a frozen copy edited by hand or truncated by a merge is detected without a network.
version_scheme.git_commit: Informative. No comparison looks at it. The sha a build can know about itself is always the one of the change BEFORE the change that contains it, so it is useless as the identity of what is published.
version_scheme.hash_completeness: Every key of the published payload is either covered or excluded, and the validator checks it. A requirement-bearing key left out of both would travel without protection: a frozen copy could be altered there and the recomputed hash would still match.
version_scheme.version_bump: Any change to a key listed in hash_covers raises catalog_version, even when no requirement changed: the content hash moves with it, and two different contents published under one declared version would make a freeze unreadable. A regeneration that only rewrites generated_at or git_commit changes nothing covered, so it leaves the version alone.
version_scheme.version_ledger: gates/catalog.json#changelog records, for each catalog_version, the content hash it produced. The build refuses to publish when the hash of the current content is not the one recorded for the current version: that is what forces the bump instead of trusting it. The ledger is append-only and a hash already recorded is never edited, for the same reason the base is not edited. It is not part of the published payload, so recording a new entry cannot change the hash it records.
version_scheme.counts_is_covered: The summary of quantities is covered by the fingerprint (since catalog_version 2026.10.6). It is derived data, and leaving it out was defensible, but a summary of quantities that can lie is worse than no summary: a tool that uses it to check it finished reading would accept a truncated file in silence. Covered, a consumer can compare counts against what it parsed and detect a short read without a second request. The same goes for `what`, which is where the file states the scope of its own protection.
version_scheme.pinning_is_covered: The pinning contract is covered by the fingerprint (since catalog_version 2026.10.7). It carries requirements -- on the consumer and on the owner -- so a frozen copy altered there would change what the project believes it owes, and the recomputed hash has to notice.

compatibility.unknown_evaluator_required: The installation does NOT report green. It reports "declared, not measured by this installation", naming the evaluator, and the step does not advance.
compatibility.unknown_evaluator_not_required: A warning: it names it and the step may advance.
compatibility.forbidden: Approximating with the closest evaluator, or ignoring the block. Zero silent damage.

since_version.note: The catalog_version in which this entry first appeared. Required on every entry that declares since_schema, which is every entry the method added after the freeze. Absent on a base entry, because the base is present in every published version.

since_schema.note: A rule of the frozen base declares none. A rule the method added later declares it, like any other entry, so that the upgrade differential can count it (D-068, D-070).

since_version.note: The catalog_version in which this rule first appeared. Required on every entry that declares since_schema, which is every entry the method added after the freeze. Absent on a base entry, because the base is present in every published version.

project_config.what: The shape of the per-project configuration that the gate reads (layer 3 of Annex H). It lives in the project, never inside a prompt (D-046), and these are the field names a consumer tool has to write and read. Declared here so no tool has to guess them.

fields.frontend: Id of the adapter family (see gates/adapters.json families).
fields.real_users: Boolean. Rules with applies_if real_users only run where it is true, and that is scope, not an exception.
fields.switches: One entry per rule group: true, or an object { on: false, reason, authorized_by, review_date }.
fields.switched_off: List of individual rules switched off, each with the full record.
fields.thresholds: Declared values, by threshold id. Whatever is not here is reported as undeclared, never invented.
fields.tools: Tool names and versions actually used, for the ruleset fingerprint.
fields.communication_depth: One of `project_config.enums.communication_depth` -- beginner, decision_maker or technical: the technical depth at which the agent speaks to the owner (UX-28). Undeclared means decision_maker, and the agent says which one it is using.

project_config.enums_what: The value list of every field above that names one, resolved here so a consumer does not have to guess it. It is not transcribed: the lists are declared once in the sources and the published block is derived from them, so a field that names an enum which does not exist is refused by the validator. Written this way on 2026-10-27: the field above said "One of communication_depth" and no key of the published file carried that name, so a tool that wanted to validate the declared depth had to guess the three values and could see only two of them mentioned in prose -- a partial list that reads as complete, which is worse than none (PND-059).
project_config.without_record: red, and the ruleset is invalid: the scoreboard emits no figures at all (D-046, D-047).

pinning.what: What a project pins, and what it costs to change it. A project pins ONE catalog_version the day it starts and keeps it until the end. That is not convenience: raising the version in the middle of a project is a REGRESSION of the completeness state, because a version that adds a requirement to a step already closed reopens that step, and what was green yesterday is not green today. Raising it is allowed and it is the owner decision, written with its date in the project decision record; what is not allowed is raising it in silence, or discovering mid-project that the gate is measuring against a definition nobody chose.

consumer_contract.must_record: A tool that pins records, in whatever it writes for the project, the catalog_version it pinned and the content_hash that version declares. Those two, by those names.
consumer_contract.must_contrast: It contrasts that pair against the version ledger: an append-only record of (declared version -> content hash) that lives in the method repository and not on the host that served this file, so the pair can be checked against a second source. Its address is published per resource by the index of this data interface, under resources[].version_ledger: url is the page a person reads and fetch_url is the same file as JSON, which is the one a tool downloads. Read both from the index; do not derive one from the other and do not hardcode either, because a derived address is an invented address. Written this way on 2026-10-27: the first wording of this clause pointed the consumer at a key of the sources that no published payload carries, and the index declared only the human page, so the one consumer that implemented the obligation had to guess the address it downloads (PND-056).
consumer_contract.on_mismatch: Red, and it says which of the two moved: the content under a declared version, or the version under one content. Never green, and never a silent re-pin to whatever the host is serving today.
consumer_contract.forbidden: Pinning to an internal compiled identity that the method cannot name. It looks like pinning and it is not: nobody outside the tool can audit it, and the differential against a published version cannot be computed, so the project cannot be told what an upgrade would reopen.
consumer_contract.why_it_is_written: Measured on 2026-10-27: a consumer that already pinned, and pinned correctly in its own terms, pinned to an identity of its own that is not a catalog_version and appears in no ledger. The data said what to freeze and never said what to freeze it BY.

upgrade.before_deciding: Compute the differential and show it: which requirements enter between the pinned version and the candidate, and which steps they anchor. A project is told what an upgrade reopens before it is raised, not after.
upgrade.how_to_compute: Every entry the method added after the freeze declares since_version. An entry with no since_schema comes from the frozen base and is present in every published version. So the differential between a pinned version X and a candidate Y is every entry whose since_version is greater than X and not greater than Y; it needs no network beyond the two files.
upgrade.what_a_new_required_evaluator_means: An installation that cannot measure a required evaluator reports declared and not measured, and the step does not advance (see compatibility). That is the mechanism by which an upgrade stops a project, and it is the intended behaviour, not a defect.
upgrade.covered_keys_note: Every top-level key the fingerprint covers has existed since the first version the method published, so no consumer can hold a pinned version that is missing one of them. A key added later records its arrival in the ledger entry of its version.

prior_version_content.immutable_url_pattern: <canonical base>/<resource folder>/<version>.json -- one folder per resource, because each resource declares its own version line and a folder named after one version would be naming the other resource's content with it.
prior_version_content.immutable_url_what: The address that returns THIS version and only this version, for as long as the method publishes. The canonical URL keeps serving whatever is current, so a tool that points at it is updated in silence and the hash moves under its feet. A project that pinned a version re-reads that exact version here, by address, instead of having to keep a copy of its own and instead of searching a repository history.
prior_version_content.immutable_url_where: Declared, never derived, and NOT in this file: the index of this data interface declares per resource the base, the address of the current version and the full list of versions that have one, under resources[].immutable. This file declares only its own path relative to that base, in immutable_path. The reason it stops there is measured and not stylistic: the data layer of this method names no tool, no protocol and no host (see the neutrality claim the method publishes with the command that counts the occurrences), and an absolute address carries the host name. A derived address is an invented address (D-069), so the absolute one is declared -- in the one file whose job is to be a directory.
prior_version_content.no_purge: Versions are never removed. An immutable address that disappears one day is worse than never having published it, because it breaks exactly whoever trusted the promise. The growth is about 165 KB per version, which is not a problem worth solving.
prior_version_content.what_is_promised: The covered payload of THAT version, not the bytes, and not more than that version's own hash covered. The keys a hash excludes are publication metadata and a regeneration can move them, so promising the bytes would be promising something the first regeneration breaks; recompute the hash and compare, which is what a consumer does anyway. And the scope is per version, measured, because the coverage grew: for this catalogue the versions from 2026.10.1 to 2026.10.5 do not cover `what` and `counts`, which 2026.10.6 closed, so for one of those versions an address can only promise what that version could prove. That is a property of a hash already published, which is never edited, and not something a later version can repair backwards.
prior_version_content.not_guaranteed: Byte identity is not promised, only the covered content, for the reason above. And an address on this host is not a substitute for the ledger: if this host is compromised, both the file and its hash can be rewritten together, so the pair (version -> hash) is still checked against the ledger, which lives elsewhere.
prior_version_content.how: The canonical URL serves the current version only. The content of a prior version is in the method repository: the ledger gives the pair (version -> content hash) and the published file is committed there, so searching that history for a recorded hash finds the commit that published that version.
